---
title: "Install R and RStudio; open your course project"
---

R performs calculations. RStudio is the application in which we write code,
inspect results, and make reports. Install both on your laptop, or use the
supported remote applications when access details are provided.

These steps are for native Windows or macOS applications. Windows students do
not need to install a second copy of R inside Ubuntu/WSL. The Linux command-line
setup is [a separate page](ubuntu-windows.qmd).

## 1. Install R

Go to [CRAN's R downloads](https://cloud.r-project.org/) and choose your operating
system. On Windows choose the **base** installation, then the standard installer.
On Mac choose the installer matching your Mac's processor and supported macOS
version; **About This Mac** identifies the processor. If the choices are unclear,
bring your computer to the setup session. Install R before RStudio.

R is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux through
[the R Project and CRAN](https://www.r-project.org/).

## 2. Install RStudio Desktop

Download the free **RStudio Desktop** installer from
[Posit](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). Choose your operating system,
install it, then open **RStudio**. You do not need to purchase a product or create
a cloud account. Check the download page's current system requirements if your
computer is older. RStudio requires an R installation, as explained in
[Posit's download guide](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/download.html).

Find the **Console** pane. Its prompt is usually `>`. Type:

```r
2 + 3
```

Press Enter. The result should be `[1] 5`. The `[1]` labels the first element
printed; it is not part of your answer or something you type.

## 3. Install the small package set

Packages add functions to R. In the **R console**, run this once while connected
to the internet:

```r
install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
```

Wait until the prompt returns. Keep installation commands out of your analysis
and report: they change the computer's setup and need not run every time.
Load packages in each new analysis session using `library()`.

If asked to compile packages from source on Windows or Mac, ask for help using
the available binary packages. Installing compilers is not a course exercise.

## 4. Download and extract the course folder

If you extracted the course folder during day 1, reuse it and continue with
step 4 below.

1. If you do not already have it, download [course-files.zip](../downloads/course-files.zip).
2. Find it in your browser's downloads, then show it in the file manager.
3. On Windows, right-click and choose **Extract All**; on Mac, double-click the
   ZIP. Move the extracted `introcomputing-course` folder to a place you can
   find again, such as Documents. Extract the whole folder, not a single file.
4. Inside the extracted folder, open `introcomputing.Rproj` in RStudio. A ZIP
   preview in Windows is not an extracted project.

Your folder should look like this:

```text
introcomputing-course/
├── introcomputing.Rproj
├── report.Rmd
├── START-HERE.txt
├── data/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── seedlings.csv
│   └── ...
├── output/
└── reports/
```

The `.Rproj` file tells RStudio which folder is this project. Data remain ordinary
files inside it. In the R console run:

```r
getwd()
file.exists("data/seedlings.csv")
```

The first result should end with `introcomputing-course`; the second should be
`TRUE`. `data/seedlings.csv` means “inside the data folder of this project”.
Keep this relative path so the project works in another location too.

## 5. Check packages and the first report

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
packageVersion("rmarkdown")
```

If these commands finish without an error, open `report.Rmd` from RStudio's
Files pane and click **Knit**. A report with a table and a growth plot should
appear. Its data are simulated. You will learn to explain and modify this report
in week 2; you are checking the installation now.

R Markdown uses Pandoc to make the output document; RStudio supplies it. You do
not need a PDF/LaTeX installation for our HTML reports.
[R Markdown's installation documentation](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/docs/)
describes these dependencies.

## If something goes wrong

| Symptom | First check |
| --- | --- |
| RStudio cannot find R | Check that R installed successfully before RStudio. |
| “There is no package called …” | Run the package installation line in the R console, then load the package again. |
| `file.exists()` is `FALSE` | Open the extracted `.Rproj`; look for an extra nested folder after extraction. |
| The console shows `+` instead of `>` | An expression is unfinished. Press Esc and check closing quotes or brackets. |
| Knit reports “object not found” | The report needs code creating the object; an object made only in the console is insufficient. |
| An installation or permissions error persists | Save the exact error and use the setup session; the remote route is an alternative once available. |

Please show the exact error and the step you reached. Do not send passwords or
authentication codes. On a managed computer, use the approved software route
with support from the teaching team.
